claims.claim: AST SpaceMobile's Q2 2026 SEC filing records successful launches/deployments of BlueBird 8-10 and the August 5 launch of BlueBird 11-13, while BlueBird 7 was lost after placement into a lower-than-planned orbit; this provides primary-source evidence of both constellation execution and launch-provider execution risk.

The August 10 business update reports approximately $1.30 billion of aggregate contracted revenue/backlog and more than 60 MNO partners covering over 3 billion subscribers, while BlueBird 17-46 were in various stages of production and assembly.

risks.risk: BlueBird 7's de-orbit demonstrates that launch-provider/orbital-insertion failure can destroy deployed capital and delay constellation density even when satellite manufacturing progresses.

unknowns.unknown: Contracted backlog does not itself establish timing, margin, collectability, or conversion into recurring service revenue.

claims.claim: Primary filings show a mixed but materially advanced execution picture: multiple Block 2 satellites reached orbit after BB6, manufacturing extended through BlueBird 46, and contracted commercial/government revenue reached about $1.30 billion, but one 2026 launch resulted in satellite loss.

risks.risk: Constellation economics remain sensitive to launch cadence, deployment success, spectrum access and conversion of contracted amounts into recognized revenue.

unknowns.unknown: This assist does not create Alpha-owned numeric underwriting or valuation conclusions.
